notes: The bridging case between the two tiers, and the same situation as eval/cases.json c02. The customer explicitly asks to move a payment and states a near-term recovery. That IS a hardship request — the staff member must establish whether it is timing or inability — and it is NOT a statutory notice, so no 21-day clock starts. Detector must emit HARDSHIP_REQUEST and no obligation. Here the staff member asks the threshold question, so the request resolves satisfied.

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: Meridian Home Loans, this is Priya. Can I get your name and the address on the loan?

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: Thanks Owen. What can I help with?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Any chance we can push the payment back a couple of weeks? I get paid on the twentieth and it's just landed awkwardly this month.

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: I can look at that. Before I do — is this a one-off, or has something changed with your income?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: One-off. Work's fine, same hours, same pay. I had a car rego and an excess land in the same fortnight and it just cleaned me out.

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: And from next month you're comfortable that the normal repayment is manageable?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yeah, no dramas. It's genuinely just this one month.

turns.speaker: staff
turns.text: Then I'll move this month's debit to the twenty-second and note the account. Nothing further will go out to you in the meantime.
